The newly focused parent company possesses a distinct product mix, margin profile, and capital structure compared to the previously consolidated business [D01, D06].

gate1.edge_statement: The event is the post-spin operational simplification of Baxter, where Third Point can apply its constructivist framework to drive margin expansion and hold management accountable for the new standalone strategy.

gate2.variant_view: The market is overly focused on transition-related overhead and macro headwinds, ignoring the inherent potential for margin expansion following the separation of the bioscience business. We believe a leaner, focused Baxter will reveal significant operational inefficiencies that a new management team can address to close the valuation gap with higher-performing peers. Success will be driven by rigorous cost discipline and a strategic reset that moves the company toward industry-standard profitability metrics.

final.memo:
Baxter International is a core medical-products and renal-care business that has recently emerged from the July 1, 2015, spin-off of its bioscience operations [D01, D07]. The market currently misprices this newly focused entity by over-weighting transition-related overhead and macro headwinds, failing to recognize the significant operational simplification opportunity now available [D04, D05].

By narrowing the focus to its core segments, Baxter has the potential to close the material margin gap existing against high-performing peers like Becton Dickinson and Danaher [D04, D06]. We project that aggressive operational focus and cost discipline can drive run-rate earnings power, supporting a path toward our $55 valuation target [D03, D04].

The market’s pessimism regarding transition costs ignores the fundamental floor provided by the company’s cash-generative medical and renal-care operations [D01, D04, D05]. We believe the current price of $42.13 offers an asymmetric entry point with a hard floor near $38 [D04].

Our plan involves private engagement with the board and leadership to force a concrete margin improvement roadmap and a disciplined capital allocation strategy [D03, D07]. We expect measurable progress toward peer-level profitability within two quarters; failure to execute will result in a rapid escalation of our constructivist efforts [D03, D07].

We are initiating a 5% position in Baxter common stock as an event-driven opportunity [D04, D05]. We intend to hedge our systemic market exposure via index puts to account for ongoing sector volatility [D04, D05].
